description.value: A reproducibility study assessed fasting-state BOLD responses to visual food stimuli in adults with overweight or obesity across two testing days.

spans.text: The purpose of this study was to assess the reproducibility of fasting-state brain responses to visual food stimuli in select reward-associated brain regions.

value: mean fasting brain responses in these reward-associated brain regions would not differ on 2 testing days with similar experimental conditions
fasting-state neural responses would demonstrate good or excellent test-retest reliability (Intraclass Correlation Coefficient ≥ 0.60)

name.value: visual food and nonfood cue task

description.value: Participants viewed blocks of visual food stimuli and neutral nonfood-related objects during fasting-state fMRI.

spans.text: Three functional runs were performed during each fMRI session. Each run consisted of 3 blocks of visual food stimuli and 3 blocks of visual nonfood stimuli presented in a pseudorandomized order using PsychoPy, Version 1.76.00 ( 24 ).

description.value: Blocks of 10 images of high-hedonic-value food stimuli, each image presented for 2.5 seconds with a 0.5-second fade; participants viewed the stimuli without a reported behavioral response.

spans.text: Each block of visual stimuli lasted 30 seconds and included 10 images presented for 2.5 seconds each with a 0.5 second fade between each image.

description.value: Blocks of 10 images of neutral nonfood-related objects, such as tools, landscapes, and household items, each image presented for 2.5 seconds with a 0.5-second fade; participants viewed the stimuli without a reported behavioral response.

spans.text: Visual stimuli consisted of images of food of high hedonic value and neutral nonfood-related objects (e.g. tools, landscapes, and household items), which were previously validated ( 17 ) and utilized in previously published reports ( 18 – 23 ).

description.value: Low-level baseline fixation-cross blocks lasting 16 seconds, presented before the first visual-stimulus block, between visual-stimulus blocks, and after the final block; no behavioral response was required.

spans.text: Blocks of a low-level baseline stimulus (fixation cross) lasting 16 seconds each were presented before the first visual stimuli block, in between blocks of visual stimuli, and after the final visual stimuli block.

caption.value: Responses to visual food cues compared to nonfood cues in the fasting-state on Day 1 and Day 2

footer.value:
1Stereotactic coordinates in MNI space for local maxima for the food vs. nonfood contrast on Day 1 within each a priori brain region of interest.

2T values reported for results of single sample t-tests for comparison of mean β coefficient of all voxels in each region for food vs. nonfood contrast to zero.

3Uncorrected P values.

Single sample Student’s t-tests (PROC TTEST, SAS, Version 9.3) indicated that visual food stimuli elicited greater brain responses compared to nonfood stimuli in all a priori regions of interest except the left putamen on Day 1 and the right caudate on Day 2. A Bonferroni correction was applied for determination of statistical significance (α = 0.05 / 10 ROI = 0.005).
Abbreviations: MNI, Montreal Neurological Institute; OFC, orbitofrontal cortex; L, left; R, right.
